Tracks every text we add to the graph and how to teach it: what practice family it feeds, what collection/journey it belongs in, and the derivation path from modern book → public source → practice. P0 = early-sutta lineage first. FoJin connector feeds parallels + dictionary + verify for every sutta row.

nanananda-magic-of-mind.title: The Magic of the Mind
nanananda-magic-of-mind.author: Katukurunde Ñāṇananda
nanananda-magic-of-mind.teach_as: practice text — read one chapter, do the signless practice the chapter describes, log what shifts

practices_to_derive.howto: Sit and notice the mind making signs — categories, images, words for what is present. Do not follow the signs; do not suppress them. Let attention rest on the bare experience behind the sign. When you notice a sign arising, note 'sign' and return to bare experience. Over time the signs thin and the concentration opens into something less constructed.
cautions: If you feel disoriented or 'unreal', open the eyes and ground in the body before continuing.
This is a concentration practice, not a void-blanket — alertness stays.

nanananda-magic-of-mind.read_order: chapter 1 → signless practice → chapter 2 → log after each sit
nanananda-magic-of-mind.fojin_check: sn-48-10-indriya: use get_parallels to find the Chinese parallel; verify any sutta quote from the book with verify_quote before shipping.

nyanamoli-dhamma-within-reach.title: Dhamma Within Reach
nyanamoli-dhamma-within-reach.author: Ajahn Ñāṇamoli Thero
nyanamoli-dhamma-within-reach.teach_as: orientation text — read the essay, sit with the practice it points to, journal one paragraph

practices_to_derive.howto: After a sit, ask: what did I take to be 'me' in that sit? What did I take to be 'mine'? Look at the answer as a phenomenon, not a truth. Write one sentence. Return to the breath. Do not argue with what you see.
cautions: This can stir existential discomfort. If distress arises, stop the enquiry and return to the breath body.

nyanamoli-dhamma-within-reach.read_order: any essay → sit → journal → next essay
nyanamoli-dhamma-within-reach.fojin_check: every sutta citation in the text: verify_quote before shipping any practice derived from it.

nanavira-tragic-comic-personal.title: The Tragic, the Comic and the Personal
nanavira-tragic-comic-personal.author: Ñāṇavīra Thera
nanavira-tragic-comic-personal.teach_as: letters, not a manual — read for orientation; no practice derived directly from letters
nanavira-tragic-comic-personal.read_order: front to back; pause on any letter that stirs something

nanananda-concept-and-reality.title: Concept and Reality in Early Buddhism
nanananda-concept-and-reality.author: Katukurunde Ñāṇananda
nanananda-concept-and-reality.teach_as: theory that underpins practice — read a section, then do the deconstruction practice it implies

practices_to_derive.howto: Take a simple perception — a sound, a feeling, a thought. Ask: what conceptual labels am I putting on this? What is there without the labels? Rest in the unlabeled experience for a few breaths. When the labels return, notice them without following. This is the deconstruction, not destruction, of concepts.
cautions: Stay gentle — this is not a war against concepts. Concepts are tools; the practice is seeing that they are made, not given.

nanananda-concept-and-reality.read_order: read one section → concept-deconstruction sit → journal

nanavira-nibbana-anatta.title: Nibbāna and Anattā
nanavira-nibbana-anatta.author: Ñāṇavīra Thera
nanavira-nibbana-anatta.teach_as: advanced reading — no direct practice derivation; pairs with the recognition work but is not the same tradition
nanavira-nibbana-anatta.read_order: after Dhamma Within Reach and one week of signless work

pannobhasa-atthakavagga.title: The Aṭṭhakavagga
pannobhasa-atthakavagga.author: Bhikkhu Paññobhāsa
pannobhasa-atthakavagga.teach_as: study text — read one verse, sit on non-clinging to views, journal

practices_to_derive.howto: Hold a view you usually take for granted — about yourself, a practice, a person. Look at it as a view, not as reality. Ask: does this view hold up? Does it serve? Do not replace it with another view. Rest in the space where no view is being held. Return when you notice yourself re-gripping.
cautions: Do not use this to dismiss all views — the Aṭṭhakavagga is not nihilism; it is non-grasping.

pannobhasa-atthakavagga.read_order: one verse per day → non-clinging sit → journal what view was being held
pannobhasa-atthakavagga.fojin_check: snp-4-11: get_parallels to the Chinese Āgama version; dictionary for the archaic Pali terms.

analayo-direct-path.title: Satipatthana: The Direct Path to Realization
analayo-direct-path.author: Bhikkhu Analayo
analayo-direct-path.teach_as: study + practice - read one section per week; sit the corresponding satipatthana contemplation; use the Chinese parallel to see what the Pali omits

practices_to_derive.howto: Sit and establish mindfulness in the body first - breath, posture, the whole body sitting. Then feelings: pleasant, unpleasant, neutral. Then mind: contracted, expanded, concentrated, scattered. Then dharmas: hindrances present or absent, aggregates arising and passing. Move through the four in order; do not skip the body.
cautions: If scanning the body triggers trauma responses, drop to the breath only and keep the eyes open.
Do not treat the four as a checklist to rush through - one establishment well is better than all four skimmed.

analayo-direct-path.read_order: section - sit one establishment - journal - next section
analayo-direct-path.fojin_check: MN 10 and its Madhyama-agama parallel: get_parallels gives the Chinese version; verify_quote for any Analayo citation we ship.

analayo-nibbana-mind-stilled.title: Nibbana: The Mind Stilled
analayo-nibbana-mind-stilled.author: Bhikkhu Analayo
analayo-nibbana-mind-stilled.teach_as: Anaylayo's 33-lecture analysis of Nanananda's Nibbana - The Mind Stilled. One lecture per session; read the corresponding section of the original Nanananda book alongside; the PDF transcript is the text; practice is the signless concentration both books describe.

practices_to_derive.howto: Read one section of Nanananda's Nibbana - The Mind Stilled. Sit and notice the mind making signs - categories, images, words for what is present. Do not follow the signs; do not suppress them. Let attention rest on the bare experience behind the sign. When a sign arises, note 'sign' and return. Over time the signs thin and the concentration opens into something less constructed. Read Anaylayo's lecture on that section; sit again.
cautions: If you feel disoriented or 'unreal', open the eyes and ground in the body before continuing.
This is concentration, not void-blanket - alertness stays.

analayo-nibbana-mind-stilled.read_order: Nanananda section 1 - signless sit - Anaylayo lecture 1 - journal; then Nanananda section 2 - sit - lecture 2 - journal; move at the pace of understanding.
analayo-nibbana-mind-stilled.fojin_check: every sutta Analayo cites: verify_quote; get_parallels for the Agama versions he references.

hareesh-vbt-translation.title: VBT Complete Translation
hareesh-vbt-translation.author: Christopher Wallis (Hareesh)
hareesh-vbt-translation.teach_as: the base translation - read one dharana at a time; sit the practice it describes; log what shifts. Pair with the blog analysis for the full picture.

practices_to_derive.howto: Sit and conceive of the body, or the whole universe, as nothing but consciousness. Let this be a felt sense, not an idea. When the mind contracts into 'me' or 'mine', return to the wider field. Rest there. This is VBT verse 63.
cautions: If this triggers derealisation, open the eyes and ground in the breath body before continuing.
This is a recognition practice, not a blank-state practice - alertness stays.

practices_to_derive.howto: When the mind leaves one object and is about to grasp another, rest in the gap between them. Do not follow the mind to its next object; do not suppress it. Stay in the middle. The highest realisation unfolds there. This is VBT verse 62.
cautions: This requires a basic level of concentration first - establish the breath gap practice before attempting.

hareesh-vbt-translation.read_order: one dharana per sitting day; read, sit, log. Start with the breath practices (24-26), progress to the middle practices (40-50), save the deep ones (52-57) for later.
hareesh-vbt-translation.fojin_check: not applicable (Sanskrit, not Pali) - use GRETIL for the Sanskrit source text.

hareesh-vbt-blog-series.read_order: blog post N - sit dharana N - journal - next post. Move at the pace of understanding.
hareesh-vbt-blog-series.fojin_check: not applicable - Sanskrit source, use GRETIL.

hareesh-vbt-concordance.read_order: as needed - when a verse is unclear, look it up

vbt-baumer-lakshmanjoo.title: VBT: The Practice of Centring Awareness
vbt-baumer-lakshmanjoo.author: Bettina Baumer tr. + Swami Lakshman Joo commentary
vbt-baumer-lakshmanjoo.teach_as: the Lakshman Joo commentary layer - his direct oral teaching on the VBT, edited from transcript by Baumer. The most direct access to how a living Trika master reads the text. Read alongside the Hareesh translation for a different angle.
